The Fifth-Generation MINI Cooper 3-Door and John Cooper Works GP Are Live, Though Only Virtually
9 photos
Photo: uygarspots / Instagram
The iconic British marque Mini has two stories: the classic and modern ones. The legendary Mini, the one we all associate with the crowded streets of London and Mr. Bean, lived from 1959 to 2000, up to the Mark VII incarnation, along with many variants.
The modern story began with the acquisition of the MINI name by the premium Bavarian automaker BMW AG to form a potent triumvirate with the MINI brand as the opening act, the namesake BMW marque as the stable housemate, and Rolls-Royce sitting at the top.
Naturally, MINI developed itself around the classic hatchback, which was reinvented for the modern age – albeit with the same signature traits. The first generation came in 2001, the second iteration in 2006, and the third one in 2013, all of them deeply and intimately connected to each other through an evolutionary design ethos.
However, the current fourth generation presented in late 2023 broke off with tradition – it’s offered both in ICE and EV form, complete with visible design changes that make it a true modern-retro offering, and it’s easily recognizable via the simpler front fascia and the triangle-shaped LED rear lights compared to the previous incarnations.
The company offers three EV flavors – Cooper E, SE, and JCW Electric plus 1.5-liter or 2.0L turbo ICE options, along with three-door, five-door, and cabrio body styles. There’s Mini John Cooper Works for both types of powertrains, of course, and you would think that’s more than enough, at least for a few years, right?
Well, wrong – as the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators won’t stop dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI any time soon. For example, Uygar, a "professional daydreamer" based in Turkey and known as ' uygarspots ' on social media, has taken note of the all-new direction of MINI with the Cooper models and opted to imagine the next generation already!
He started fresh with a daring reinterpretation of the iconic model – the virtual artist keeps the overall shape along with the round headlights and the Union Jack motif of the taillights, but makes the MINI Cooper look ready for the 2030s. It’s all in the ‘pixels’, clearly, as now there are pixel-shaped round headlights, a pixel grille, as well as pixel-infused wheels and roofs!
The three-door model is also much wider now, giving space to a potential double-opening rear hatch – and you can also see the much larger Union Jack (British flag) LED taillights firmly occupy the space. The pixel master posts a few variants, as MINI always equals personalization, but more importantly, he comes back to also reveal his vision for the John Cooper Works GP, a true hot hatchback, even if it’s all electric.
